newsitem.title: PERU: Peru withdraws Uruguay diplomat after siege swap.
newsitem.headline: Peru withdraws Uruguay diplomat after siege swap.

text.p: The Peruvian government withdrew its top diplomat in Uruguay on Wednesday after Montevideo's release of two alleged Peruvian rebels appeared to win the freedom of their ambassador in the Lima hostage crisis.
"We can confirm we have withdrawn the chief of mission of Peru in Uruguay," a Foreign Ministry official told Reuters.

The official, who asked not to be named, would not comment on the reason for the withdrawal on Wednesday of Efrain Saavedra, who was Peru's leading diplomat in Uruguay. Saavedra was deputizing for Peru's ambassador to Uruguay, Guillermo del Solar, who was absent for family reasons.
However, Lima's decision appeared to be a protest at Tuesday's release by Uruguay of two alleged Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) members.

Peru's President Alberto Fujimori has been unflinching in refusing to consider the demands of rebels holding 105 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima that the government free their jailed comrades.
Peruvians were angered at the surprise release from the besieged residence of Uruguay's ambassador, Tabare Bocalandro, only hours after the releases in his country.
While all other releases of healthy hostages in the eight-day old siege have been in groups, Bocalandro left the residence alone.
Montevideo officially claimed the two events were a coincidence, but a well-placed Uruguayan government source told Reuters a deal had been struck.
A Uruguayan appeals court ruled on Tuesday that two MRTA members held in connection with the 1995 kidnapping of a Bolivian businessman be freed.
The court ruling revoked a decision in May to uphold a Peruvian extradition request against Luis Alberto Samaniego and Silvia Gora Rivera.
Bocalandro's release from the Japanese ambassador's residence reduced to 105 the number of hostages, including government officials, Japanese VIPs and some foreign diplomats.
